elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Section 4.9 as amended reads "no more than once per year" and Section 7.4 retains "no more than once each Calendar Year". "Calendar Year" is defined as January 1 to December 31, so two inspections could occur within a rolling 12-month window (e.g. December and the following January); neither clause states "once in any 12-month period".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Both amended clauses require "at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice", short of the 30-day preferred standard.
Section 4.9 retains "during normal business hours", but Section 7.4 inspections remain permitted merely "at reasonable times" with no business-hours limitation.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Section 7.4 uses an "independent certified public accounting firm ... reasonably acceptable to Ono", but Section 4.9 permits Array itself "and/or an authorized representative" to inspect — not an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 7.4 requires the Auditor to "execute a reasonable confidentiality agreement", but the Section 4.9 inspection by Array or its authorized representative carries no equivalent confidentiality undertaking in the operative text.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: Section 4.9 expressly requires Ono to "permit Array ... to enter the relevant facilities of Ono and its Affiliates"; no off-site-where-possible qualifier was added anywhere.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Section 7.4 as amended shifts cost only where underpayment exceeds "ten percent (10%)", not 5 percent.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Section 4.9 still grants on-site entry plus "the right to examine any internal procedures or records of Ono and/or its Affiliates" with mandatory assistance; no exclusion of direct access to Ono systems/records was inserted.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Section 4.9 now reads "during normal business hours, no more than once per year"; Section 7.4 already limits inspections to "no more than once each Calendar Year" with one inspection per calendar quarter. Both audit rights binding Ono are frequency-capped at once a year.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Section 4.9: "upon at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice"; Section 7.4: "on at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice". Both replace the former open-ended "reasonable" notice standard.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Section 7.4: "Inspections conducted under this Section 7.4 shall be at the expense of Array, unless a variation or error producing an underpayment in amounts payable exceeding ten percent (10%) ... is established". The blank "[ * ]" is fixed at exactly the fallback threshold. Section 4.9 is a regulatory-compliance inspection with no payment-verification function, so the underpayment cost-shift condition does not apply to it.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the once-per-year cap, the 15-day prior written notice (inserted in both the Section 4.9 facility inspection and the Section 7.4 records inspection), and the 10% underpayment cost-shift are all in operative language, not merely promised in the comment.

Preferred level fails on multiple elements: notice is 15 days rather than 30; Section 4.9 still permits Array itself (rather than an independent auditor) to enter facilities without a confidentiality undertaking; there is no off-site-where-possible qualifier; the cost trigger is 10% rather than 5%; and direct on-site access to Ono's facilities, internal procedures and records is preserved. Section 7.4 also remains at "reasonable times" rather than business hours, and both clauses use a calendar-year rather than any-12-month cap.

Minimality holds: the edits are three targeted insertions (frequency cap and 15-day notice in 4.9, 15-day notice in 7.4, 10% in the previously blank "[ * ]" threshold). Favourable existing language — independent accounting firm, Ono's reasonable acceptance, the Auditor confidentiality agreement, Array-bears-cost default, one inspection per quarter, minimise-disruption undertaking — is retained untouched, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, remedies) were added.

Intent is preserved: the interest cross-reference to Section 7.1, the three-year records retention period, the GxP/regulatory purpose of the Section 4.9 inspection and the "shall not relieve Ono of any of its obligations" sentence all survive without contradiction; no defined term is left dangling and "Calendar Year" and "Auditor" remain intact.

Deviation classification is correct on the original text: notice was open-ended "reasonable" in both clauses, Section 4.9 had no frequency cap at all, and the cost-shift threshold was left blank, so the fallback was not met on material terms before the redline.

If the team later wants the preferred position, the operative repairs are: raise notice to 30 days in both clauses, lower the Section 7.4 threshold to 5%, add "in any twelve (12) month period" in place of the calendar-year measure, subject Section 7.4 inspections to normal business hours, require Section 4.9 inspections to be conducted by an independent representative under a written confidentiality undertaking, and add an off-site/records-copy-first preference limiting direct access to Ono facilities and systems.
